title: Typical residual samples cannot replace global structural coverage
statement: On the n-spin cube with h=1,uniform guide and auxiliary gap2, a uniformly hidden spike V_z(x)=a n 1{x=z},a>1 has every fixed typical absolute moment tending0 while lambda_max(Q+V_z)>=(a-1)n. Adaptive value queries hit the spike with probability<=q/2^n; the reported uniformly valid confidence(1-gamma) spectral-density interval of width<a-1 requires q>=(1-2gamma)2^n for gamma<1/2. Whole one-spin-neighborhood queries improve coverage only by their size. This is a value-oracle obstruction for a NONLOCAL potential, not hardness for explicit sparse pair interactions or the supplied star. It identifies missing global information without granting a learned sector or certificate from typical data.

requires: L=sum_(i=0..n)(X_i-I)+sum_(i=1..n)J_i Z0 Zi, with0<Jmin<=Ji<=Jmax<infinity fixed independently of n; bath spins are independent conditional on the central spin, whose degree is n.
Known analytic product sectors p_+,p_-, exact global spin-flip symmetry and positive unique top eigenvector; actual inverse-excitation moments use the exact conditional bath spectral law.

Source model/sector parameters and full structural coverage are supplied. Extending to genuinely interacting conditional sectors requires earning the retained subspace and leakage spectral moments at actual acquisition/validation cost.

Companion rate/local/oracle results retain their own scopes and do not inherit the star review. All P3 no-upload/no-export/no-repackaging/no-alternate-transfer restrictions persist. O(n) scalar work is not O(n) bit-time, analytic sectors are not freely learned, the local chain bottleneck is not intrinsic sampling hardness, and fidelity requires the separate symmetry/leakage argument rather than a narrow energy interval. costs: Classical construction uses O(n) scalar sums/products and polynomial exact-arithmetic costs for the implemented rational inputs, not O(n) bit-time or an optimized arbitrary-precision error solver.

An equally informed ordinary global sampler draws a fair central spin then independent conditional bath spins in O(n). The explicit cat has bond dimension2; ordinary methods receive the same sectors/compact representation.

Ideal state preparation costs1H,n single-spin rotations and n central-controlled gates; shared central control gives O(n) sequential depth without extra architecture. Rotation synthesis/access and noise are additional resources.

Bravyi–Gosset already supplies polynomial energy approximation for a broader ferromagnetic family containing this star. The previous Vuong/degree3,s=.1 comparison remains at the predecessor fixture; it is not silently transferred to the degree-n star.

The1025-spin rational certificate is producer-reported, not independently replayed here. The target is a supplied mathematical Hamiltonian, with no physical calibration or device fidelity measurement.
